--- description: "The shared dsh core: model access, tools, durable sessions, and safety defaults for every dsh --profile surface, for users composing or customizing a profile." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-base English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Every base-backed `dsh --profile` surface runs on `dsh-base`, so those surfaces share a model connection, the full tool set, durable session history, and workspace safety defaults. The shipped `sdk-minimal` profile deliberately uses a complete standalone tree instead. You rarely touch this bundle directly — shipped base-backed profiles already include it, and a custom base-backed profile names it first. When you need different defaults, change your profile patch or add a later bundle; this package is not a library you import. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package You get the dsh core automatically: the shipped `web`, `headless`, `sdk`, and `acp` profiles already include it, and a custom profile names it as its first bundle. After that, everything works with no further configuration. ### A minimal custom profile To build a profile on the shared core, create a profile with a `package.json` that names `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` first: ```json { "name": "my-profile", "private": true, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base"] } } } ``` Run `dsh --profile my-profile "your task"` and you get a working agent with model access, tools, persistence, and the default permission policy. The shipped `web`, `headless`, `sdk`, and `acp` profiles are created for you on first use. To add more bundles, run `dsh plugin --profile add `; in-box bundles resolve from the dsh installation. The profile contract is documented in the [app-boot profile section](../../boot/app-boot/README.md). ### What you get Out of the box, every profile built on this core provides: a DeepSeek model connection (the provider and model are configurable, and you can enable extra providers from your settings), the full tool set — file editing, shell commands, web search, public HTTP(S) fetch, subagents, task and goal tracking — durable sessions that survive restarts, and the default permission policy that confines file writes to your workspace and asks before risky actions. Web fetch runs without per-call approval; its provider rejects non-public destinations. Feedback stays in the Session log. [OTel session upload](../../session/session-telemetry-otel/README.md) defaults to `FEEDBACK_ONLY` for all users, including `deepseek-official`: new text feedback, message ratings, edits, and withdrawals release the complete canonical prefix through that event, including context. Later records wait for the next explicit feedback; sending an authorized batch needs no further interaction or model call. `DISABLED` prevents OTel capture. The default-on [DeepSeek session-log contributor](../../session/session-log-deepseek/README.md) remains a separate request path. Default file editing uses `read`, `write`, and `edit`. The `str_replace_editor` tool remains available as an explicit opt-in. To add it to a base-backed profile, put this entry in the profile, home, or invocation patch: ```yaml - insert: - id: tool-str-replace-editor name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor' config: maxOutputChars: 16000 ``` The bundle mounts [MCP resources](../../mcp/mcp-resources/README.md) once. Configure only [MCP client entries](../../mcp/mcp-client/README.md) for the servers you need. Clients mounted by another provider also count as configured in their scope. Callers with no configured server in scope receive no MCP tools or prompt text. ### Shell tools per platform On macOS and Linux you get the bash shell tools; on Windows you get the PowerShell twins instead, so exactly one shell stack is available per machine. The safety behavior is identical on every platform. A Windows host that prefers the unconfined PowerShell executor can switch the shell rows in its profile patch — the switch must disable both PowerShell rows and re-enable both bash rows, otherwise the profile fails to load. ### Changing the defaults To change what a profile built on this core provides — a different default model, a stricter permission mode, extra or fewer tools — edit your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` or add a later bundle. Each patch entry replaces the target's whole configuration, so restate every setting you want to keep. Keep the sandboxed filesystem provider as the single file-write path: adding the plain filesystem provider on top of it makes the profile fail to load. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The bundle is a static patch document: one `insert` list applied over the empty profile root. It mounts no service, emits no events, and holds no mutable state; each inserted row's package owns that row's behavior and invariants. ### Composition mechanics A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config` rather than merging into it. Later bundle layers and the user's profile `cordis.patch.yml` override rows by id, with the last write winning per row. Rows whose value differs by mode do not live here: each mode bundle restates its complete configuration, keeping any single row down to one bundle layer plus the user's. The full row set and its rationale are documented inline in [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml); the [generated composition graph](../../../apps/cli/composition.md) renders it. ### Platform gating The patch gates the two shell stacks by platform on its own rows: `bash-sandbox` and `tool-bash` carry `disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'`, and their twins `pwsh-sandbox` and `tool-pwsh` mount on win32 only with the inverted expression. The permission surface stays identical to POSIX: the sandbox policy executes the same file-effect policy through the Windows ACL restricted-token runner (`dsh-sandbox-local` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`), and `fs-sandbox` keeps fencing `ctx.fs` writes — mounting `dsh-fs-local` alongside it would double-register `ctx.fs` and fail the load. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The bundle substance: the base plugin rows, with per-row rationale as inline comments | | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Package entry; carries no runtime API | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; the package is a static patch-list carrier (a YAML document of loader rows owned by other packages); it mounts no service, emits no events, and owns no mutable relation to check. Each inserted row's own package carries that row's invariants. | | [`tests/base.spec.ts`](tests/base.spec.ts) | Manifest declaration and platform-gating checks | ### Invariant ownership No invariant companion is published because the package is a static patch-list carrier: each inserted row's package owns that row's invariants, and the bundle owns no mutable relation to check.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want to go deeper into profiles, the surfaces built on this core, or the exact composition. - [app-boot profile section](../../boot/app-boot/README.md) — how profiles are resolved, layered, and customized. - [Bundle package map](../README.md) — the surfaces built on this core. - [Generated composition graph](../../../apps/cli/composition.md) — the exact plugin set each shipped profile uses. - [Profile plugin bundles note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-05-profile-plugin-bundles.md) — the profile and bundle composition design. - [Codex and Claude Code provider bundles](../../subagent/README.md) — optional provider bundles you can install on top. ----- ## Model Experience Indirectly, through each inserted row's package, which owns that row's model-facing behavior. #### KV Cache effect The bundle itself adds no request prefix; each inserted row's package owns any cache effect. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits tell you when the core needs extra care or where an override must go. They are current package constraints, not a general comparison or a task backlog. - **Overrides replace whole settings blocks** — a patch entry replaces the target's entire configuration, so your override must restate every setting you want to keep; nothing merges automatically. - **Per-surface settings belong to the surface's bundle** — a default that differs between the web GUI and headless mode lives in that surface's bundle, not in the shared core. - **Windows temp grants are private per-session subdirectories** — `workspace-write` confines writes to the workspace plus the session's own temp subdirectory (`\dsh-`, TMP/TEMP rewritten for confined children); `read-only` grants nothing. See `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`. - **Adding the plain filesystem provider on top of the sandboxed one fails the profile** — the two register the same service, so the profile refuses to load; use one or the other. ### Dev Note

--- description: "One-shot task mode for dsh: run a single task from the command line and get the final answer printed, for users scripting or automating dsh." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-headless English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary `dsh-headless` runs one dsh task from the command line and prints the final answer, then exits — no GUI, no server, no browser. Type `dsh --profile headless "run the tests"` and the agent handles it with the same model, tools, and safety defaults as every other surface. It suits scripts, CI, and one-off jobs: it opens no ports and leaves nothing running behind. It also offers a JSON event stream (`--json`) and `--session-id` to resume a conversation. Exit code 0 means the task completed; 1 means it aborted or errored. The boundary: one task per invocation, no interactive follow-up. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Run one task, get the final answer, and exit. The task is the command-line argument, or stdin when you omit it; the whole invocation is the smallest working example. ### Running a one-shot task ```sh dsh --profile headless "run the tests" ``` The agent works through the task, streams each non-empty provider reasoning delta to stderr under a `dsh: reasoning:` heading, then prints the final answer on stdout and exits. Consecutive reasoning deltas stay in one section, and the runner closes that section before later output when the provider supplied no trailing newline. A successful run without reasoning keeps stderr empty; a failure exits 1 and prints `dsh: : ` to stderr. The task comes from the positional argument, or from stdin when the argument is omitted or is a lone `-`; a blank positional argument or an empty pipe is rejected before anything runs. A positional task is used as-is and stdin is not read, so put the whole prompt in the pipe when you want piped input; a piped task is sent verbatim, its trailing newline included. ```sh { echo "Summarize these changes:"; git diff --stat; } | dsh --profile headless ``` The task and run options are supplied through three settings: | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `task` | stdin | The task text; stdin supplies it when omitted or `-` | | `sessionId` | `session-` | Exact Session identity to adopt; an unknown id fails | | `json` | `false` | Project the run as newline-delimited events on stdout | The generated [configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-headless) is the exhaustive source for every accepted field and its JSDoc. ### Choosing the session identity Every invocation defaults to a fresh `session-` identity, which `--json` reports in its opening `session` event. Pass `--session-id ` to continue that conversation: the runner adopts the persisted Session with that id, and an id with no stored Session fails before the task runs rather than quietly opening an empty history. Adoption requires the composed `sessionPersistence` and `sessionQuery` services, so a profile that omits either fails loudly instead of returning an id whose history dies with the process. An Agent already live under the requested id in this process is refused: another owner may still drive it, so the runner cannot claim an exclusive run interval over it. The identity is opaque, so the exact string is used, whitespace included. The working directory is resolved through the mounted filesystem provider (`fs.resolve('.')` and `fs.processPath()`), or the process cwd when no filesystem service is mounted; new Sessions record that directory. Adoption compares the recorded cwd with the same provider-resolved directory and refuses a Session that is a subagent or forked session, that recorded no working directory, that runs under an agent preset this profile does not compose, or whose preset record is malformed — the check reads the preset the Session log currently records, so a Session that switched preset while blank is rejected too. A supervisor therefore cannot silently drive someone else's conversation under a different composition; any mismatch fails before the task runs. ### Machine-readable output `--json` replaces the final-text stdout line with a newline-delimited JSON event stream, while stderr keeps only the `dsh:` diagnostics. The stream opens with `session` (carrying the identity the run used) and closes with `final`, and carries `status`, `text`, `thinking`, `tool_call`, and `tool_result` events in between. `text` and `thinking` are projected from committed assistant messages, so a retried or discarded attempt never reaches the stream; they arrive when the step commits, not per token, and default-mode stderr reasoning remains the only live text channel. The terminal `final` event carries the same lossless answer as the default mode and is not capped; every other string and object key is capped at 8 KiB and flagged with `truncated`, and one event line, its newline included, is capped at 32 KiB — an over-long event keeps its scalar fields, drops structured ones, and at the extreme reduces to `type` and `truncated`, while a payload nested 64 levels or deeper is cut at that depth. An empty tool-argument string projects as `{}`, matching what the executor runs, while arguments that JSON cannot round-trip — an overflowing number such as `1e400` — keep their raw text rather than the `null` that `JSON.stringify` would report. A failure the runner raises outside a turn writes an `error` event and ends the stream without `final`, in addition to the `dsh:` stderr line; a profile whose own plugins fail to load exits before the runner mounts, so that case keeps only the loader's stderr diagnostics. A turn that fails in-turn still ends with a `final` event (often empty) and no `error` event, so a well-formed stream can still describe a failed run: treat exit code 1 and the `turn_end` reason as the failure signal. ### When to use it Use headless for scripted or automated dsh runs — CI steps, batch jobs, quick answers from a terminal. Avoid it when you need a multi-turn interactive session or a GUI; the browser surface ([dsh-web-app](../web-app/README.md)) serves that. The process stays alive only for the run, opens no listening port, and exits on its own, so it fits pipelines that wait on the process. When a supervisor needs progress rather than just the answer, `--json` gives it the event stream and `--session-id` lets a later invocation continue the same conversation. ### Help and task errors `dsh --profile headless --help` prints the command's help text and exits without running anything. A whitespace-only positional task is a usage error on its own — nothing runs and the process exits 1, even when stdin is not a terminal, so an accidental blank argument never consumes a pipe. A task that is absent entirely is a usage error only when stdin is a terminal; otherwise the runner reads the task from stdin and rejects an empty result the same way. A lone `-` is the only stdin marker; mixing it with other task words is a usage error rather than a task that starts with a dash. In `--json` mode every usage error — including commander's own grammar rejections such as an unknown option or a missing option value — also writes an `error` event to stdout before the process exits, so a line-oriented supervisor sees a well-formed stream even when the runner never mounts; the event `message` carries the text without commander's `error: ` prefix. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The runner is a direct driver over the core API carrier: it resolves the Agent identity — a fresh `session-` by default, or the persisted Session `--session-id` names — and folds the owned durable event interval into one process-level outcome. ### Run flow The runner awaits the complete application (`ctx.get('loader')?.await()`) so the composed tools and adapters are not half-mounted, reads the shared [`agentDefaultModel`](../../core/agent-default-model/README.md) selection, resolves the task from config or stdin, then resolves the Agent identity: a fresh `session-` by default, or the persisted Session `--session-id` names, which it adopts through [`sessionQuery`](../../session-query/session-query/README.md) and refuses when no log exists. It submits the task as an ordinary user message. Without `--json` it streams that Agent's non-empty reasoning deltas to stderr; with `--json` it projects the run instead. It waits for quiescence, then flushes the Session and folds the owned interval (`firstSeq` onward) into the last non-empty `assistant/message` text and final `turn/end` reason. It writes the final text to stdout (or the `final` event) and requests exit. ### Patch surface over base The patch rides over `dsh-base`: it inherits the projection cache and shared PTC runtime, sets the coding persona prefix and separate cwd suffix on the base `system-prompt` row, keeps the same temporary process-wide PTC mode opt-in (`DSH_TOOLS_MODE`) as the Web surface, disables the shared HMR row, and mounts the startup provider and the runner. The cache checkpoints each persisted one-shot session for later consumers; its durability barrier flushes each covered log prefix before publishing the cache row and may split otherwise coalesced JSONL runs. The startup provider ([`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts)) injects `ctx.cmdlineArgs` ([`dsh-cmdline`](../../boot/cmdline/README.md)), reads the positional argument and the `--session-id`/`--json` options, prints the app's `--help`, and provides `headlessStartup`; the runner injects that service and reads its task and run options from lazy config. ### Exit mapping A completed final `turn/end` exits 0; any other outcome — aborted, error, or no turn in the owned interval — exits 1. An `error` reason also writes `dsh: : ` to stderr. A direct driver failure (for example, Agent creation or an unusable `--session-id`) writes `dsh: ` to stderr and exits 1, and in `--json` mode also emits an `error` event. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | The `headless-runner` plugin: run flow, session resolution, output contract, exit mapping | | [`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts) | The `headless-startup` provider: task positional, `--session-id`, `--json`, and `--help` | | [`src/json-stream.ts`](src/json-stream.ts) | The `--json` projection: event vocabulary, commit-point emission, string bounding | | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The one-shot patch over `dsh-base` | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; the runner's observable contract (provider reasoning on stderr, final text on stdout, exit code by turn-end reason) is process-level and owned by the launcher e2e; it registers nothing and holds no mutable relation to audit inside the tree. | | [`tests/headless.spec.ts`](tests/headless.spec.ts) | Run flow, aggregation, flush, session adoption, and exit mapping | | [`tests/json-stream.spec.ts`](tests/json-stream.spec.ts) | Projection ordering, commit-point emission, bounding, and disposal | | [`tests/startup.spec.ts`](tests/startup.spec.ts) | Command-line parsing over a real Loader tree | ### Invariant ownership No invariant companion is published because the runner's observable contract (final text on stdout, exit code by turn-end reason) is process-level and owned by the launcher e2e; the plugin registers nothing and holds no mutable relation to audit inside the tree.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want to go deeper into the shared core, the sibling GUI, or the command-line handoff. - [Bundle package map](../README.md) — the surfaces built on the same core. - [dsh-base](../base/README.md) — the shared core headless runs on. - [dsh-web-app](../web-app/README.md) — the interactive browser sibling for multi-turn work. - [dsh-cmdline](../../boot/cmdline/README.md) — how the launcher hands the command line to the app. - [Generated configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-headless) — every accepted config field and its source declaration. ----- ## Model Experience None, as the runner submits the task as an ordinary user message and the composed base and headless rows own the prompts and tools. #### KV Cache effect The runner adds nothing to the request prefix; it only drives one user message through the composed tree. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits tell you when headless does not fit and what it needs from the `dsh` launcher. They are current package constraints, not a general CLI comparison or a task backlog. - **One task per run** — after the task is answered the process exits; there is no interactive follow-up, so split multi-step work into separate runs. - **Runs through the `dsh` launcher** — starting the headless profile another way fails at startup, because only the launcher can request the process exit. - **No pre-token heartbeat** — in default mode stderr stays silent until the provider emits a non-empty reasoning delta; a delayed first token exposes no earlier progress signal. - **Reasoning enters stderr logs** — in default mode, redirection and supervisors may retain substantially more and potentially sensitive model output; route stderr to a controlled sink when needed. - **Default stdout carries only the final answer** — a run without an assistant message prints an empty stdout line and exits 1; intermediate tool output is not printed unless you opt into `--json`. - **Adoption is cwd-, ownership-, and preset-scoped** — `--session-id` refuses a Session recorded in another working directory, one that recorded no working directory, one that is a subagent or forked session, or one that runs under an agent preset this profile does not compose or whose preset record is malformed, and requires the composed Session query and persistence services; an identity already live in the process is refused too, because the runner cannot own an exclusive run interval over it. - **The event stream is a projection, not the log** — `--json` caps every string except the terminal `final` at 8 KiB and omits events the projection does not model, so it is not a lossless copy of the Session log. ### Dev Note

# DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseek-harness2026, title={DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, publisher={GitHub}, howpublished={\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness}}, } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-image-preview > [中文版](./README.zh.md) **Image preview for the dsh session interface.** dsh 0.2.x already renders `read_image` as a collapsed image card and assistant final-output images as an official gallery. This plugin takes over all of them: `read_image` rows get a **thumbnail visible by default**, and images the user sends, plus images in the assistant's final answer — including image files in `present` delivery cards — use the same **full-size lightbox** with cross-image navigation, zoom, rotate, pan, download, and file actions (open with default/associated app, open in sidebar, reveal in folder). ## Features | | | | --- | --- | | 🖼️ **Visible thumbnail** | `read_image` results render as a rounded ~240px thumbnail instead of a collapsed card, so the image is visible without expanding the row | | 🔍 **Click for full size** | Click the thumbnail to open the original image in a lightbox — dismiss with `Esc`, clicking the backdrop, or the close button; focus is restored to the trigger on close | | ↔️ **Cross-row navigation** | Arrow buttons / ← → keys cycle through **every image loaded in the session** (counter shows `3 / 4`) — dsh's built-in lightbox only ever shows a single image | | 🔎 **Zoom, rotate, pan** | Toolbar with zoom out / zoom in / rotate left / rotate right / download. Scroll wheel zooms, drag pans while magnified, and `+` `-` `0` `,` `.` are keyboard shortcuts. Zoom is clamped to 25%–800% and resets when you switch images | | ⬇️ **Download** | Saves the original bytes under the attachment's own filename through a same-origin `` (works with the `blob:` URLs the host loader returns) | | 🔐 **Uses the host's image pipeline** | Image bytes are resolved through the session-authorized `loadImage` loader dsh injects into the slot owner — no hand-rolled attachment RPC | | 🧾 **Final-output images** | Assistant image blocks (`conversation.chat.message.images`) and Markdown images in the final answer open the plugin lightbox too | | 👤 **User-sent images** | Images in the user's own message (`conversation.chat.user.images`) are taken over too and open the plugin lightbox | | 📂 **Presented image cards** | Image files in `present` delivery cards (e.g. `preview_hero.png`) open the plugin lightbox directly instead of the sidebar first; STL / Markdown cards keep the official preview | | 🧩 **0.2.x-aware** | Shadows only the row renderer; the official `tool.call.images` child slot stays declared and untouched | | ⏱️ **Complete states** | Running (`row.running`), failed with retry (`image.loadFailed`), and loading (`image.loading`) states are all covered | | 🌗 **Theme aware** | All colors reference dsh theme tokens (`--dsw-*`), so the preview follows the light/dark theme automatically | ### Lightbox controls | Action | Control | Shortcut | | --- | --- | --- | | Zoom in / out | toolbar `+` / `−`, or scroll wheel | `+` / `-` | | Reset view | click the zoom percentage | `0` | | Rotate | toolbar ↺ / ↻ | `,` / `.` | | Pan | drag (only while magnified) | — | | Download | toolbar ⤓ | — | | More actions | toolbar ⋯ | — | | Previous / next image | side arrows | `←` / `→` | | Close | ✕, backdrop, or `Esc` | `Esc` | ## Compatibility Built and verified against **dsh `0.2.1-rc.2`**. The browser contract is unchanged from `0.1.5-rc.2`; the plugin is still a pure client bundle with no host-side behavior. The manifest declares `engines.dsh: >=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` so dsh can reject it outside that range. **What changed in dsh 0.2.x.** dsh now ships its own `read_image` toolview, image card, and `tool.call.images` child slot filled by the official `MessageImages` gallery. The official row is **collapsed by default**, and its lightbox shows one image at a time. This plugin still shadows the whole row so thumbnails stay visible, and keeps the extra lightbox features. It deliberately does **not** declare `tool.call.images` as a child: the official entry already declares that slot, and a second declaration would throw `slot ... is already declared`. Image positions include the user message slot `conversation.chat.user.images` (official `MessageImages` at priority 100, shadowed at -1) and the assistant final-output paths. Assistant image blocks go through the `conversation.chat.message.images` single slot, which this plugin shadows at `priority: -1` (the official `MessageImages` uses `priority: 100`). Markdown images (`![alt](path)`) are rendered by a private button/lightbox inside `MarkdownText`, not a slot, so the plugin intercepts clicks in the capture phase and opens its own lightbox. `present` delivery cards are not a slot either: the whole-card preview button's `title` is the Host absolute path, and the plugin intercepts only image extensions; STL / Markdown cards still open the official sidebar preview. If the host does not expose a ReactDOM render root, all interception backs off and leaves the official behavior intact. `read_image` submits **PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF** only, so those are the formats the plugin can display; earlier claims about SVG / BMP / ICO were incorrect. > **Why the low priority matters.** `tool.call.toolview` is a **keyed** slot, and its registry rejects a second registration for the same key at the same priority: > > ``` > keyed slot "tool.call.toolview" already has an entry for key "read_image" > at priority 0 — register at a different priority to shadow it (lowest renders) > ``` > > So this plugin registers at **`priority: -1`** to take over the shipped row. Without that, `apply()` throws during client boot and **not a single row renders** — which is exactly what happened before this fix. ## Preview **Feature overview** — user images, `read_image` tool rows, assistant images, Markdown images, and `present` delivery cards all share the same lightbox: ![Feature overview](docs/overview-en.png) **In-session thumbnails** — every image starts as a thumbnail; click to open the plugin lightbox: ![In-session thumbnails](docs/preview-en.png) **Plugin lightbox** — cross-image navigation, zoom, rotate, pan, download, and the “More actions” menu at the far right of the toolbar: ![Plugin lightbox](docs/lightbox-en.png) **File actions for presented images** — default app / associated apps / open in sidebar / reveal in folder: ![File actions](docs/actions-en.png) > Screenshots and illustrations by Alger. ## How it works `dsh-image-preview` is a **pure client-side plugin**. It registers a keyed slot on `tool.call.toolview` with key `read_image` at `priority: -1` and takes over rendering of the `read_image` tool row: ``` agent runs read_image └─ tool result content: [{ text envelope }, { type: "image", attachment }] └─ tool-call node → tool.call.toolview (key = read_image, priority -1 shadows the shipped row) └─ ReadImageRow: thumbnail + click to open the cross-row Lightbox ``` - `sessionId` and `t` are injected by the session-scoped slot's standard kit (`dsh-client-ui-session` / the locale seat). - `loadImage` is the session-authorized loader dsh passes in the slot owner props (`MessageImageLoader`, i.e. `uiConversation.imageUrl(sessionId, attachment)`, cached per session). The plugin never touches `/api/session.attachment` directly. - Attachment metadata (`attachmentId`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) comes straight from the tool result block. - The lightbox looks like dsh's built-in `ImageLightbox` (portal to `body`, backdrop mask, ESC/backdrop/close dismissal, focus restore) but adds cross-image navigation plus zoom / rotate / pan / download. - Zoom and rotation are a single CSS `transform` on the `` (no re-encoding); downloads hand the loader's `blob:` URL straight to ``, so no bytes are copied or re-fetched. - The image registry is bucketed by `sessionId`, so two sessions open at once never cross-navigate into each other's images. Final-output images: ``` user message → conversation.chat.user.images (single slot, priority -1 shadows MessageImages) assistant content ├─ image block → conversation.chat.message.images (single slot, priority -1 shadows MessageImages) │ └─ MessageImagesRow: thumbnail + click to open the same Lightbox ├─ Markdown ![alt](path) → private MarkdownText button │ └─ document click capture → plugin Lightbox (standalone React root) └─ present delivery image → [data-presented-file] > button[title] (Host absolute path) └─ document click capture → plugin Lightbox (standalone React root) ``` The `⋯` menu at the right edge of the lightbox toolbar offers local-file actions for images with a host path: open with the default application, choose from associated applications, open in the right sidebar, or reveal in the file manager. It uses dsh's Session Remote (`openWorkspacePath` / `workspacePathApplications`) and `sidebarRight.openResource`; the Host revalidates the path before launching anything. ## Installation dsh 0.2.x uses separate profiles for the desktop app and the CLI web surface. Pick the one you actually run: - **Desktop app:** `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` (reserved for the app). - **CLI web:** `~/.dsh/profiles/web`. ### Desktop app Open the in-app **Plugins** page (sidebar) and install `algerkong/dsh-image-preview` from GitHub, then enable the bundle and restart the app. Alternatively, fully quit the app first (the profile is locked while it runs) and use the CLI: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add 'github:algerkong/dsh-image-preview' ``` `add` only installs the dependency. Enable the bundle in the Plugins page, or append `"@alger-ai/dsh-image-preview"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`, then restart the app and refresh. ### CLI web ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add 'github:algerkong/dsh-image-preview' ``` Then append the package to the existing `dsh.profile.bundles` array in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` (keep the bundles already listed): ```json { "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "@alger-ai/dsh-image-preview" ] } } } ``` Run `pnpm install` in the profile, restart `dsh web`, and refresh the page. ### Manual install Add the dependency to the profile's `package.json`: ```json { "dependencies": { "@alger-ai/dsh-image-preview": "github:algerkong/dsh-image-preview" } } ``` Then add `"@alger-ai/dsh-image-preview"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, run `pnpm install`, and restart the surface. ### Local development Link the package directly: ```sh cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop # or ~/.dsh/profiles/web pnpm add link:/path/to/dsh-image-preview ``` Add `"@alger-ai/dsh-image-preview"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, restart, and refresh. ## Usage 1. Start a session and let the agent call `read_image` on an image file. 2. The tool row shows a small thumbnail by default (the official row would stay collapsed). 3. Click the thumbnail to inspect the full-size original in the lightbox. ## Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm test # node verify.mjs ``` `verify.mjs` checks three layers: the `__ModuleLoader__.load` registration shape, the **keyed-slot takeover contract** (it reproduces dsh 0.2.1-rc.2's keyed + `children` declaration rules and fails if the plugin forgets `priority: -1` or re-declares `tool.call.images`), and an actual render pass over the component (loadImage path, thumbnail, lightbox, Esc, multi-image grid and navigation, plus the zoom / rotate / download toolbar). The self-check resolves React from the repo devDependency, then from `DSH_REACT_PATH` or a DSH profile. Missing React is an error; set `DSH_VERIFY_ALLOW_SKIP=1` only when you intentionally want to run the first two layers alone. ## Files ``` dsh-image-preview/ ├── package.json # bundle metadata (dsh.bundle.patch / dsh.client platform=web) ├── pnpm-lock.yaml # devDependency lock (self-check only; not part of the bundle) ├── cordis.patch.yml # registers the client entry (id: ui-image-preview) ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # host-side entry (empty — browser-only plugin) │ └── client.js # browser: read_image row + final-output images + lightbox └── verify.mjs # self-check script ``` ## License MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH-modelspec

A [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) web-client plugin. It reads the
[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) catalog, compares it against the models a deployment
configured, and writes the differences back.

The panel is the **Model specs** entry in the left sidebar, laid out as the harness's own
**Settings → Models** page: one card per configured provider route, one editable row per model
inside it, and the specification fields behind a disclosure. What this panel adds is the
comparison — every field carries the value the catalog publishes for it, beside the value the
deployment stores — and the actions that adopt it into the same editor.

Repository: [AmakiSora/DSH-modelspec](https://github.com/AmakiSora/DSH-modelspec). See
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for what has changed in each release.

## What it does

- **The card is an editor, not a report.** A row's fields hold staged values. **Apply** writes
  what the card changed in one settings write, **Cancel** discards it, and a card with unsaved
  edits says so. Nothing is written on a keystroke, and a field that ended up where it started
  costs no write at all.
- **Compares only what you configured.** The adapter directory publishes every route an LLM
  adapter knows about — pi-ai alone ships three dozen — so a route appears only when its
  settings namespace resolves a profile that declares at least one model.
- **Never writes a preset.** A route the adapter ships itself (`deepseek-official`,
  `deepseek-account`, pi-ai's own catalog routes) is compared but never written. The rule is
  the directory's own `declared` answer, not a list of names, so it tracks whatever the
  installed DSH considers a preset. A preset card is read-only throughout.
- **Shows how confident each match is.** An entry located by identical model id is named
  differently from one reached after dropping a vendor prefix or ignoring punctuation, and the
  row says which comparison found it.
- **Refuses to invent.** A field the catalog does not publish is never proposed, and a model
  with no catalog entry at all is reported as unmatched rather than guessed at.

Fields covered: context window, max output tokens, accepted input modalities, and reasoning
efforts. The effort comparison only runs where the deployment's namespace family accepts the
field — pi-ai routes, in practice — and only when the catalog entry publishes efforts, which
OpenRouter does for the models whose endpoints name them.

## The card editor

Each provider card carries its model rows the way the harness's Models settings does:

- the model id and display name on the row, with a tag saying how many stored values the
  catalog contradicts, a **Pinned** tag when the entry was chosen by hand, a disclosure for the
  specification fields, and the removal action;
- behind the disclosure, context window and max output as text fields, the accepted input types
  as checkboxes, the reasoning-strength declaration, and the catalog entry the row is compared
  against with the button that changes it;
- **Add model** below the list, and **Apply** / **Cancel** beside the card's head once anything
  is staged.

The values are the deployment's own; the catalog's published value sits under each field it can
fill, with an **Adopt** action that stages it. Nothing about adopting writes: the reader sees
the value in the field and commits the card when they mean to.

A field cleared in the editor is written as an `unset`, which hands it back to the adapter —
the only meaning "unset" has for a value the deployment may never have written itself. Only the
fields an edit actually changed are addressed, so opening a card and applying it unchanged
writes nothing.

**The panel opens clean.** A card only shows unsaved edits when the deployment itself disagrees
with what a fresh draft would write, so a route configured by hand — a reasoning dict without
an `off` level, a model declaring no input types — is ordinary configuration rather than a
pending change.

## Adopting published values

- **One field:** the **Adopt** action beside the published value fills that field.
- **One model:** the match line's **Adopt** fills every field the entry publishes.
- **One card:** **Adopt published values** in the card's head fills every row of the route.
- **Every card:** **Adopt all differences** in the header writes every value the catalog
  contradicts, one settings write per namespace. It is disabled while any card holds staged
  edits, so a bulk write never lands on top of a draft.

Each of the first three stages values; the fourth writes. That split is deliberate: the card is
where a reader decides, so the only write it can perform is its own **Apply**.

## Catalog entry per model

The disclosure's match line names the entry the row is compared against — either the automatic
match, with the comparison that found it, or the entry the reader pinned. **Change entry** opens
the dialog that picks one, searches the catalog, offers the fuzzy comparison on demand, and can
fill the card from the chosen entry at the same time.

**The entry source is a panel preference, not deployment configuration.** The settings document
validates every write against the adapter's own schema, which declares no field for it, so the
binding is kept in this browser's local storage instead — keyed by host, route, and model id,
so two deployments on one machine stay apart and reordering a route's models re-points nothing.
A pinned entry the catalog no longer publishes falls back to the automatic match rather than
leaving the model unmatched. A model whose id an edit renamed takes its binding with it.

## Reasoning efforts

A pi-ai model entry that declares no `reasoningEfforts` is served as a non-reasoning model, and
the harness UI offers no reasoning-strength selection for it. The row's reasoning block
therefore mirrors the adapter's own vocabulary: a switch for the declared level list, one row
per level pairing it with the wire spelling sent to the provider, and a **Non-reasoning model
(writes false)** checkbox for the outright declaration.

A level left with an empty *off* value means "supported, sends no parameter" and is written as
`off: null` — but only when the entry actually declares `off`. An entry that never declared it
keeps it undeclared, because that is the difference between "cannot stop reasoning" and "stops
by sending nothing". A staged declaration that offers no level beyond `off` is refused before
the write, mirroring the rule the adapter's own resolution enforces.

## Adding a model

**Add model** on a card opens a dialog that asks for a model id and fills the rest.

- **Fetch available models.** A button beside the id field asks the route's own provider what it
  serves, so a model can be added without knowing its id in advance. The question goes to the
  Host, which is where the answer is: an adapter that already describes the route answers from
  its own catalog without touching the network, and a gateway or self-hosted route is
  interrogated at the endpoint its profile declares — `{baseURL}/models` for an
  OpenAI-compatible protocol, the Messages listing for an Anthropic one — using the route's
  stored credential, which never reaches the browser. Every id the endpoint answers with is
  offered with what it disclosed about name, context, output, and input types; one the route
  already configures is shown and marked rather than offered. A provider that serves a few dozen
  models is the ordinary case, so the listing carries a search field that narrows it by id or
  name as you type — and forgets the query when a fresh listing is requested, because the ids
  that narrowed the last answer would leave the new one looking empty. Taking an id fills the
  fields and asks the catalog about it, so the comparison below stays in play. A field the
  endpoint stayed silent about is left to the adapter, and a name that only repeats the id is
  not stored.
- **One entry matched.** The published values fill the fields and the dialog names the
  comparison that found it. The new model then follows that entry — the browser-local entry
  source the row editor also writes — so its row is compared against it from the moment it
  exists; an id no entry answered for follows its id instead.
- **Several entries matched.** Every one is offered, with the provider it came from and the
  capacities it publishes, and nothing is chosen until you pick. The same precedence a
  comparison uses decides which entries are offered at all: the resolved provider first, then
  every provider, and a loose comparison only once the precise ones found nothing. An entry
  chosen here replaces whatever the endpoint disclosed, because that entry is what the row will
  be compared against.
- **Nothing matched.** **Fuzzy search** asks the looser question — which published ids came
  close — and offers them nearest first, each labelled with *why* it was offered: identical
  once folded, one id containing the other, or *n* characters apart. A mistyped character, a
  truncated paste, and a dated variant all land here, because every comparison needs an exact
  relationship. It is a button rather than something every keystroke pays for: the edit budget
  is one character for a five-to-eight-character id, two for a longer one, and none below that,
  where one edit would reach most of the document. The route's own provider breaks ties.
- **Still nothing.** The dialog falls back to a default template built from the models that
  route already configures — the last one that declares a capacity donates its values and its
  namespace's modality field — and says so.

The fields are editable, and the confirm button answers the route's own rules rather than the
catalog's: an id the route already configures, or a capacity that is not a positive integer, is
refused with the reason shown. Enter submits from the id field.

The write itself is one path-addressed `set` at the first index past the end of the namespace's
`models` array, which is how the settings document appends. The address is that array's own
length rather than the number of rows the panel shows, so an entry the panel could not read is
never overwritten. The namespace revision guards it, and a refusal leaves the dialog open with
what you typed.

## Removing a model

**Remove** is the one control with no shortcut back: it takes the entry out of the deployment's
configuration, and putting it back means adding it again. It is an icon rather than a text
button, and it asks first — the confirmation names the model, says whether the provider keeps
other models, and warns that removing a provider's only model takes the provider off the panel
entirely.

The settings document has no delete verb, so the write is an `unset` at the array index — the
one edit that takes an element out and shifts the ones behind it. The panel therefore re-reads
its rows afterwards instead of trusting the index it held when the button was pressed, and the
namespace revision guards the write against another window having reordered the array
underneath. The entry binding goes with the model it described rather than lingering as hidden
state for an id the route no longer stores.

## Requirements

Dsh `0.2.1-rc.2` or later. The plugin is built against the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`
packages at that version and relies on the web shell's client module table. Installing it needs a
profile whose app supplies the plugin manager — the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` plus web app
do — because the plugin is installed as a bundle rather than by editing the profile by hand.

## Build

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build      # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown emits lib/index.js and lib/client.js
pnpm run test
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
```

`pnpm run build` produces the runtime artifacts, and `cordis.patch.yml` ships beside them as it
is written:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/index.js` | node half — an empty `apply()`, present so the host Loader can import the package |
| `lib/client.js` | the browser bundle the shell loads |
| `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` | type declarations |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | the bundle layer: the one row a profile composes |

## Install into a profile

The package is a dsh **bundle**. It declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and ships the `cordis.patch.yml`
that inserts its own row, so installing it selects the layer that puts the panel in a profile's
composition, and no patch is written by hand.

Install `dsh-modelspec` from the Web sidebar's **Plugins** page. The `plugin_manager` tool's
`install_bundle` and the `dsh plugin` command do the same thing. Then open **Model specs** in the
sidebar; a live profile recomposes on its own, a startup-only one needs a restart.

**Install from the registry, not from the repository.** A published package carries the built
`lib/`; a checkout does not — `lib/` is gitignored, and nothing builds it during a git install. A
`github:`/`git+https:` address therefore installs a package whose node half is missing, and dsh
reports `Cannot find module …/dsh-modelspec/lib/index.js` when it activates the row. Install
`dsh-modelspec@1.0.0` (or a later version) by name. A path or tarball is only a valid alternative
when it points at a **built** package — the staged directory below, or `pnpm pack` output.

**Selecting the bundle and writing the insert by hand are alternatives, not steps.** A profile
that has an `- insert: - id: dsh-modelspec` block of its own — every install before this bundle
layer existed — composes the row a second time once the bundle is selected. Remove the block, or
leave the bundle unselected.

### When a profile cannot import the panel

dsh loads a plugin's node half from the profile's own `node_modules`, so an install that left the
package without `lib/index.js` surfaces as one warning at activation and nothing on the page:

```
dsh: warning: 1 entry did not activate dsh-modelspec (dsh-modelspec): failed to import:
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
'…\.dsh\profiles\<name>\node_modules\dsh-modelspec\lib\index.js'
```

Three installs produce it, and the profile's `package.json` tells them apart:

| `dependencies["dsh-modelspec"]` | What happened | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"link:C:/Users/<someone-else>/…"` | the profile was copied from another machine, and the link points at a directory that does not exist here | point the value at this machine's staged directory, or reinstall by name |
| `"github:…"`, `"git+https://…"` | the repository was installed, and a checkout ships no `lib/` | reinstall from the registry by name |
| `"^1.0.0"` (or another range) but `lib/` is absent | the package directory is incomplete — an interrupted install, or a store that lost it | remove and reinstall the plugin |

`dsh-modelspec` from the registry always carries `lib/index.js`, `lib/client.js` and
`cordis.patch.yml`; check any install with `dir …\node_modules\dsh-modelspec\lib`. A profile that
was copied between machines also needs `bundles` in its `dsh.profile` and the `link:` path
rewritten to the directory that machine actually has — see below.

### A local build instead

`pnpm run stage` copies the artifacts and the patch into `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-modelspec` and
writes a dependency-free manifest there. That directory is what `install_bundle` accepts as a
path; a profile can also be pointed at it by hand:

`~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/package.json`

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-modelspec": "link:C:/Users/<you>/.dsh/plugins/dsh-modelspec"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-modelspec"]
    }
  }
}
```

Four names are one identity: the staged manifest's `name` is the dependency key, the staged
directory is the path that key points at, `tsdown.config.ts`'s `PACKAGE` is the id the browser
bundle registers under, and the shipped patch's inserted row is the entry a profile composes.
Rename them together or the profile and the bundle stop agreeing; a profile that already
installed the plugin needs its dependency key and bundle selection updated by hand.

Earlier installs of this panel were named `model-aid`. After renaming, a profile's
`package.json` and `cordis.patch.yml` need the new key and id, and the old
`~/.dsh/plugins/model-aid` directory is no longer read. Entry sources a browser had pinned
under the old name are carried across on first use, so nothing is silently unpinned.

Use `node scripts/stage.mjs --out <dir>` to stage somewhere else.

## How the browser bundle is shaped

The shell loads a client plugin's `lib/client.js` itself, so the artifact has to match a
contract this project cannot change from the outside:

- CommonJS wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`. The shell hands the
  factory a `require` bound to its own module table.
- The nine specifiers in `SHARED_MODULES` (`tsdown.config.ts`) stay imports, so the plugin
  shares React, Cordis, and the ui-primitives / ui-slots / client-store runtime identities
  with the shell rather than inlining private copies.
- Every other bare specifier is inlined. A `require` the module table cannot answer would
  throw when the factory runs.
- `*.module.css` is compiled at build time by lightningcss and injected as a tagged `<style>`
  when the factory executes, default-exporting the hashed class map the components import.

The `dsh-modelspec-bundle-purity` tsdown plugin rejects any other `@deepseek-ai/` value
import at build time. Cross-plugin behaviour goes through Cordis services and slots, not
imports.

## Releasing

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/),
which is what makes the next version mechanical to read off the history:

| Commit | Version bump |
| --- | --- |
| `fix: …` | PATCH |
| `feat: …` | MINOR |
| `feat!: …` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer | MAJOR |

Other types (`docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `chore:`, …) carry no bump on their own. A scope
may follow the type — `feat(picker): …` — to name the part of the codebase a change belongs
to.

Each release then gets a section in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) written for a reader rather
than generated from the log: the `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` / `Removed` categories from
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), an ISO date, and a `vX.Y.Z` tag.

Publishing is the tag push: `.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs the specs, checks that the tag
names the version in `package.json`, and publishes from the runner — which is not behind the
network the registry is unreachable from here. Running `pnpm publish` in a terminal does the same
thing when the registry *is* reachable. Either way `files` decides what the tarball carries and
`prepublishOnly` rebuilds before it is packed, so a version cannot be published from a stale
`lib/` — the mistake that ships a manifest whose imports do not exist. The workflow needs one
repository secret, `NPM_TOKEN`: a granular token with **bypass 2FA** enabled, since a run cannot
answer a one-time-password prompt. The version in `package.json`, the changelog section
describing it and the tag are the same number;
[tests/release.spec.ts](tests/release.spec.ts) is that checklist, executable.

The project is on `1.0.0`, which under [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) is the promise
that the panel's behaviour is depended on: from here an incompatible change is a major bump, not
a minor one.

## Layout

```
src/index.ts                 node half (empty apply)
src/client/index.ts          apply(): sidebar entry + main panel + change subscriptions
src/client/catalog-service.ts browser-side catalog read, TTL cache, single-flight
src/client/catalog.ts        OpenRouter document parsing and indexing (zod)
src/client/match.ts          configured route/model → catalog entry, and the fuzzy search
src/client/configured.ts     settings namespaces → configured routes and models
src/client/comparison.ts     differences between stored and published values; write ops
src/client/draft.ts          the editor's staged values, their refusal rules, and the write that commits them
src/client/bindings.ts       which catalog entry each model follows, kept in this browser
src/client/add-model.ts      default template, the appending edit, and the draft rules
src/client/store.ts          panel state, write planning, write execution
src/client/ModelsDevPanel.tsx   the panel: header, provider cards, dialogs
src/client/ProviderCard.tsx     one route: head, model list, add and apply
src/client/ModelRow.tsx         one model: identity, disclosure, catalog entry
src/client/ModelFields.tsx      the capacity, modality and reasoning fields both surfaces share
src/client/CandidateList.tsx    the id field and entry chooser both dialogs share
src/client/AddModelDialog.tsx   the add-model dialog
src/client/EntryDialog.tsx      the catalog-entry dialog
src/client/RemoveModelDialog.tsx the removal confirmation
src/client/CatalogSettingsDialog.tsx the catalog address dialog
src/client/locales.ts        zh + en dictionaries
cordis.patch.yml             the bundle layer: the row a profile composes
tests/                       the specs: matching, write paths, bindings, the editor, and the panel
.github/workflows/publish.yml the tag push that publishes the version to npm
CHANGELOG.md                 one section per release, written for a reader
AGENTS.md                    the versioning, commit and changelog conventions
LICENSE                      MIT
```

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# 设计与代码的建模/自动化审查（dsh-model-everything）

English · 中文

把设计与代码里的断言抽象成模型，交给引擎跑一遍：结论带出处与哈希，能复算、能比对。让结论来自一次运行，而不是一次通盘推理：把「想清楚」变成「跑一遍」。 DeepSeek Harness 原生插件。把设计与代码里**关于行为的断言**变成可运行、可审查、可导出的模型： - **核验断言**：逐条对着源码检查，引用到 `file:line`。 - **跑模型**：状态机、协议、多机协作、数据模型先建成可执行模型，再交给引擎跑。 - **审图**：UML 图按模型读、按模型审，并与模型对照。 - **对照重构**：重构前后各建一份模型，两份报告摆一起比。 - **留痕**：结论固化成带哈希的报告，可复算、可比对、可导出。 ## 能力范围 | 域 | 做什么 | |---|---| | 事实核验 | 把一份设计/规格/评审意见里的可验证断言列出来，逐条对着代码核验并给出出处。核不了的直接说明 | | 行为验证 | 状态机与协议：结构检查、对抗性探测、预算与时限、before/after 回归。多机组合查死锁，以及永不发生的会合（握手事件） | | 图 | UML 2.5 各图族的渲染、解析与建模审查（含 render→parse 往返一致性对照），覆盖 Mermaid 与 PlantUML 两种记号 | | 结构 | 组件/包/类/部署图按依赖图审计：孤立节点、悬空引用、环、矩阵与分层违规、缺失的必需边 | | 数据 | 数据模型与迁移：结构、迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称、前后数据回归 | | 并发 / 同步 / 异步 | 挖掘"工作怎么被执行"的断言（线程安全、锁、中断、async/await、事件循环…）并路由到能判定它的工具；它自己不证明 | | 导出 | 已验证模型导出为 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的输入 | | 报告 | 报告正文渲染、基线比对（`report_diff`）、哈希规范 | ## 典型用法 ### 重构 harness 重构可以改实现，不能改行为。这个判断交给引擎，不必通读 diff： 1. **重构前**：从当前代码抽出 BEFORE 模型（`uml_parse` 读已有的图，或按 schema 手写）。 2. **重构**。 3. **重构后**：抽出 AFTER 模型。 4. **回归**：`model_verify` 带 `beforeModel` 与 `stateMapping` 跑前后回归：行为是否保持、不变式是否连续、状态映射是否自洽。数据侧用 `model_datamodel_verify` 的 `beforeModel` / `fieldMapping` / `migrationMappings` 做同一件事的**数据版**。 5. **判定与留痕**：`report_diff` 拿基线报告比对。新增的 error 发现，就是这次重构不接受的理由。报告里的哈希让结论可复算。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**，不是两份代码。每份模型是否忠实于对应代码，由第 1、3 步负责，它不代替你做。它也不读 diff、不改代码、不跑你的测试。它回答的是"行为还一样吗"，不是"重构得好不好"。 ### 代码流程审查 先把分支逻辑画成流程，再看这张图到底说了什么： 1. **抽流程**：把函数或服务里的分支写成 `LogicModelV1`，或者手画一张 `stateDiagram-v2` / PlantUML 图。 2. **读回模型**：手画的图交给 `uml_parse` 转成模型。读不动的行会变成警告，不会悄悄跳过。 3. **审查**：`uml_review` 报结构缺陷——不可达状态、死端、分支有歧义或没穷尽、自环没有出口、孤立节点、环——以及文档缺口。 4. **落回源码**：每条发现都回到代码核验。图画对了，不等于代码写对了。 它审的是你给的那张图和那份模型。图与代码是否一致，由第 1 步的抽取负责。 ### 状态机审查 把状态机建成可执行模型，让引擎去跑，而不是通读代码判断它会不会卡死： 1. **建模型**：手画的 `stateDiagram-v2` 或 PlantUML 状态图交给 `uml_parse`；也可以直接按 schema 写 `LogicModelV1`。 2. **跑检查**：`model_verify` 找的是不可达状态、吸收环、被静默忽略的事件、没有恢复路径的资源申请、预算超限，以及无法满足的时限。每一项都作为一个**带码**的发现报出，而码的前缀说明它属于哪一族。 3. **写清"永远/绝不"**：把这类断言写进 `invariants`，引擎会在全部可达状态上搜反例，并给出它找到的最短路径。 4. **落回源码**：报告里的 error 发现逐条回到代码。 并发断言分两半：**两个模型都碰同一个共享位置**这一类，由我们自己的 `model_compose_verify` 判（声明 `shared` 与 `accesses` 之后的 C3/C4/C5，包括丢更新）；源码级数据竞争、中断延迟、阻塞调用与漏掉的 `await` 仍路由到 TSan/Helgrind/CBMC/TLA+。硬实时语义（deadline、period）不在它的范围内。 ### 审计一张依赖图 组件图是关于「哪些模块可以依赖哪些」的断言。把它当图读，再问那些边是否被允许： 1. **给图**：PlantUML 的组件/包/类/部署图源码，或 Mermaid 类图。`uml_structure_verify` 把它解析成节点与边。 2. **说清什么被允许**（如果有规则）：一个含 `layers` 与 `rules` 的矩阵，每条规则点名一个 `source` 并给 `allow` / `deny` / `require`，再用 `default` 管其余。没有矩阵时，它只报结构缺陷。 3. **读发现**：孤立节点、从未声明过的端点、带最短路径的环、越过层的边、缺失的必需边，以及——一个节点都没声明时——**这份输入没有任何可审的东西**。 4. **换一种图就换个工具**：如果这张图是状态图或活动图，那是 `uml_review`，不是它。 它审的是**图**，不是代码。一张自洽的图仍可能画错了系统，所以要和源码侧扫描配对。手画的图报「标签漂移」时，`uml_explain_labels` 会打印该记号下解析器接受的标签写法。 ### 让设计对自己作出的声明负责 设计会对自己作出断言：这一层在那层之上、这个组件拥有那条依赖、这个接口比它的调用方窄。`model_design_review` 判定设计是否守住了这些承诺： 1. **把设计写成模型**：架构（节点与边），加上它声明的——分层、边界、允许与必需的边、带职责的类型、操作、转移、父类型。 2. **跑它**：`model_design_review` 报出设计与自相矛盾的地方，并**另外**报出它图的形状——环与打断环所需的最少边、承重元素、层级、扇入扇出。 3. **读那三个列表**：`violations` 决定判定；`signals` 值得一看但不使任何东西失败；`facts` 是**测量**，不是发现。`checksSkipped` 说明哪些原则因为**没声明任何可对照的东西**而没有检查。 **它从不按外部标准评判设计。** 它报的是：设计**与它自己声明的某件事**矛盾，或关于它的图的一个结构事实。问「这个设计好不好」是评审者的问题；这个工具回答的是另一个：**它就自己的说法而言，站得住吗**。 ### 两台必须互相配合的机器 一台机器**不会因为另一台**而死锁。当两个组件握手时，真正有意思的失败在**组合**里： 1. **各自建模**，然后一起给：`model_compose_verify` 收一个模型数组。 2. **点名共享事件**：如果一个握手只有在双方都就绪时才合法，把它写进 `rendezvous`。没写进去的事件只推进一台机器，所以等握手的机器可以先走任意多步自己的路。 3. **读 C1 与 C2**：一个可达节点上没有任何机器能前进、且有机器不是终止态（C1），以及一个**永远不会触发**的会合（C2）。两者都逐机给出理由，C1 还给最短反例。 模型里**没有速率比，也没有公平性约束**。单台机器自己的问题——不可达状态、不变式、成本对预算——用 `model_verify`。 ### 并发声明：挖掘并路由 「线程安全」「lock-free」「ISR 安全」都是需要某个能判定它们的工具的断言，而第一步是**把它们找出来**： 1. **扫文本**：`model_interleaving_scan` 收文档、计划或笔记，报出风险点——那条声明、共享状态、中断、临界区，以及异步的那些（`async`、`await`、`promise`、事件循环、回调）。每条发现都带 `family`（threads / synchronization / async / interrupts / shared-state），绝对式断言按 error 报。 2. **看每条绝对声明欠着什么**：「不可能有数据竞争」这类声明会被报为 error，要求**专门的**验证，且每条发现都点名能判定它的分析——竞争用 TSan 或 Helgrind，有界证明用 CBMC，协议用 TLA+，中断用 RTOS 感知的分析。 3. **去做那个分析**：本插件不运行它，也不对并发安全作任何证明。 它读的是**文本**。它看不见你的线程，而**一次干净的扫描不是健康证明**——它的含义是没找到声明，这是另一个命题。 ### 一次迁移：前后两份模型 迁移是两份模型，加一个「数据活下来了」的断言。把两份都给出去，这个断言就变成可核查的： 1. **两份模型**：改动前的 schema 与改动后的 schema，各自是含实体、字段、键与关系的数据模型。 2. **说清字段怎么走**：`fieldMapping` 从旧路径到新路径，加上 `migrationMappings`——用于来源不是它自己旧名字的字段。 3. **跑比对**：`model_datamodel_verify` 带 `beforeModel`，检查迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称，以及前后数据回归。 4. **读那条警告**：新 schema 里声明为 `required`、却没有任何东西供给它的字段，会报 `DS2_REQUIRED_FIELD_UNSOURCED`。它是 **warning**，所以判定停在 `pass_with_findings`——**这是一个要做的决定，不是引擎可以替你宣布的失败**。 它比较的是**你给的两份模型**。任一份是否忠实于它所描述的数据库，是抽取那一步的事，这个工具不做。 ### 图的导入与导出：设计冻结与长期迭代 这里存的是**源文件**，不是截图：`uml_render` 写出 Mermaid / PlantUML 源，`uml_parse` 把源读回模型。一份图因此能当两种东西用： - **设计冻结的留档**：把图源、模型和那一次的验证报告一起提交进仓库，作为某个时间点的设计记录。模型里可以放 `_` 前缀的元数据（单据号、日期、负责人、抽取时留下的保留意见），这些键不参与哈希，补档案信息不会改变结论的身份。 - **长期迭代的参考**：下一次改动时重新抽出模型、重跑验证，再用 `report_diff` 与冻结的那份报告比对。新增的 error 是这次改动引入的，消失的说明旧问题已经解决；哈希让"还是不是同一份模型"可判定，不必肉眼比图。 需要交给外部检查器时，同一份模型可以用 `model_export` 导出成 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN 的原生输入。 界线：它保存并比对的是**模型与图的源文件**，渲染出来的图片只是副产品。图变了模型没变、或模型变了图没变，都会在下一次解析或比对时暴露。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 做什么 | |---|---| | `uml_render` | 模型 → 图源（Mermaid / PlantUML），可指定图族。记号表达不了的视图会被拒绝，并说明理由 | | `uml_parse` | 图源 → 该图族的模型；不属于状态机/流程的族会按名拒绝，而不是硬当作状态机解析 | | `uml_review` | 审查建模：结构缺陷、文档缺口、render↔parse 往返一致性；给模型、给图，或两者对照 | | `uml_explain_labels` | 打印解析器接受的标签与注释契约，不需要图 | | `model_verify` | 状态机 / 协议的可执行验证（结构检查、对抗性探测、预算、时限、前后回归） | | `model_compose_verify` | 两台及以上机器的组合检查（死锁、永不发生的会合；声明了共享位置后还有无序写 C4 与非原子更新 C5） | | `model_datamodel_verify` | 数据模型与迁移验证 | | `model_interleaving_scan` | 并发 / 同步 / 异步声明的挖掘与路由 | | `model_export` | 导出到外部检查器（UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN） | | `uml_structure_verify` | 依赖图审计（含依赖矩阵与多层级细化） | | `model_design_review` | 设计审阅：依赖图形状 + 设计自身声明的契约（分层、职责边界、可替换性、接口宽度） | | `report_diff` | 两份报告比对：新增/消失/变化的发现 | ## 怎么读报告 工具的产出是一份报告，结论只在 `verdict` 里：**看 `verdict`，不看 `ok`**。`ok` 在各族的含义不同——多数族在评审失败时仍是 `true`，组合族在出现 error 级发现时是 `false`——所以它不能当判定读；把它当判定读，会得出与报告相反的结论。 | 字段 | 说明 | |---|---| | `verdict` | 判定：`pass`、`pass_with_findings`、`fail` | | `verdictReason` | 一句话说明为什么是这个判定 | | `hashes` | `hashSpec` 与 `modelHash`；前后回归另带 `beforeModelHash`、`afterModelHash`。同一份模型永远得到同一个哈希 | | `nextSteps` | 引擎建议的下一步 | | `schema` | 报告的版本化契约，例如 `model-everything/verify/v1`。要按字段分支，就分支在它上面 | | `truncated` | 搜索撞到上限就停了。**截断不等于通过**，是没结论；某个性质没判定出来时，报告里会出现 `_UNDECIDED` | 默认返回正文。要完整 JSON，传 `reportView: "full"`。 `ok` 为 `false` 时判定也是 `fail`，但含义不同：工具根本没跑。原因写在 `errorCode` 里——输入不合法、图族不支持，或声明的 `intent` 服务不了。这类拒绝的 `verdictReason` 以 `the tool did not run:` 开头。 报告怎么读，有一份成体系的说明：[`skills/model-everything-report-reading/`](skills/model-everything-report-reading/) 讲阅读顺序（先看跑没跑、再看判了什么、最后看该做什么）、发现分别放在哪一层、以及两处最容易读反的地方。结构由一个**从真实报告生成的思维导图**给出：[`docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd`](docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd)，`tests/report-reading` 会在图与引擎不一致时失败。 `uml_render`、`uml_parse`、`uml_review` 另收一个 `intent`，用来说明这份产物要做什么：给人看（`present`）、要被验证引擎读回（`verify`）、还是要证明渲染与模型一致（`fidelity`）。服务不了这个用途的视图会被直接拒绝，而不是勉强画出来。 ## 示例 `examples/` 里是可以直接跑的样本模型，配 model=examples/control-dispatcher.json ``` ## 技能 技能按域拆分，讲的是怎么用、按什么判定： | 技能 | 覆盖 | |---|---| | `model-everything` | 入口：断言清单、核验纪律、深度分级、到各域技能的路由 | | `model-everything-uml` | UML 图：选哪种视图、标签约定、审查码、往返一致性检查的边界 | | `model-everything-structure` | 架构与依赖：矩阵怎么写、各条结构检查意味着什么 | | `model-everything-datamodel` | 数据模型与迁移：不变式（任何时刻都必须成立的约束）、迁移覆盖、回滚对称 | | `model-everything-design` | --profile add dsh-model-everything # 未全局安装 dsh 时 npx -p @deepseek-ai/dsh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-model-everything ``` 装完重启该 profile，`dsh --profile --dump-config` 里应能看到本插件的行。卸载同样走插件管理器，从目标 profile 移除。 技能走 DSH 标准的 filesystem skill provider 注册，工具挂在 `ctx.tools` 上。另有一条模型可见的状态目录条目，可查注册状态与引擎接受的 schema 版本。 ### 两个组件 | 组件 | 行 id | 做什么 | 默认 | |---|---|---|---| | `dsh-model-everything` | `dsh-model-everything` | 全部工具与技能 | 开 | | 提示词注入增强 | `dsh-model-everything-gate` | 会话第一条模型步注入一条路由提示 | 开 | **提示词注入增强**是第二个组件，单独开关。它补的是路由的短板：路由靠技能描述文字，而目录行截断在 500 字符；更要紧的是，一次会话如果压根没决定加载技能，就没有任何东西把它路由过去。 它在每个会话注入一条消息（约 3.2k 字符），内容四块：不确定该查哪个时先加载哪个技能、每个技能管什么、每个工具做什么以及**它不证明什么**、以及怎么读一份报告（`verdict` 而不是 `ok`，`skip` 不是 `pass`）。**那条"先加载技能、别凭记忆回答"的规则在开头说一次、结尾换个说法再说一次**——这是量出来的：只说一次时，那种"觉得自己会答"的请求（迁移）既没加载技能也没用工具；首尾各说一次之后它补上了，而对照任务没有被过度触发。 它的形状借了同一个 harness 里另一个插件往系统提示注入的那一节的三招（那套做法在本环境里已有先例）： - **只广播装得上的东西**：技能表按 `skills/` 目录里真实存在的技能渲染，所以表里不会出现一个解析不到的技能名；新加技能若还没写行，会退回"see its catalog line"，**可以不全，但不会指错**。 - **选择表而不是一句话清单**：`| 这个请求 | 这个技能 |` 两列，路由本来就是在近义项之间排序，表格比散文更像一道选择。 - **反降级规则**：工具拒绝时读 `errorCode` 改输入再试；工具没装就明说并退回通用方法——**没有任何东西跑过的检查不是通过的检查**。 它怎么工作，四句话： - **注入点**：`agent/pre-step`，把消息追加到该会话**第一个**模型步的决策里，不是 session-start——后者落进 inbox，可能被空会话的 preset 切换清掉； - **只注入一次**：消息带自己的 producer source kind，每一步都按会话历史查一次，见到就不再注入；被清掉的话会在下一个能跑的步重新出现； - **开关**：`enabled` 是 live 字段，插件页翻开关对运行中的 host 立刻生效；`gateContent` 不是 live（一千多字的散文不该进表单），要改写在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里；`extraGuidance` 是留给部署自己加一句的追加槽； - **它只路由**：不检查任何东西，也不会让技能自己加载。 **开关与默认**：默认开。这个默认值是量出来的——它补上的是插件唯一接不住的那类请求，而对照任务没有被过度触发。代价是每个会话约 3.2k 字符；要关掉就改 `cordis.patch.yml`（见下）或翻插件页的开关。想做对照（同一个请求，关一次开一次）也用它。 `gateContent` 可以整段替换，用来试别的措辞；`tests/gate` 仍要求它点名每个已发布的技能。 ## 配置 注入组件（默认开）有三个键： | 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 | |---|---|---|---| | `enabled` | boolean | `true` | 是否注入。live 字段：插件页翻开关对运行中的 host 立刻生效，不用重启。 | | `gateContent` | string | 内置文本 | 注入的全文。替换它等于自己写路由规则；`tests/gate` 仍会要求它点名每个已发布的技能。 | | `extraGuidance` | string | `""` | 追加在消息最后的一段话，留给部署写自己的规则。 | 主行只有一个 `interaction`（提议调用工具时怎么处置，默认 `follow-approval`）；关掉主行是关掉那一行本身，不是改配置。 按 row id 写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`： ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-model-everything-gate name: 'dsh-model-everything/gate' config: enabled: false # 关掉注入 ``` ## 边界 - **不拥有你的代码。** 只读必要的文件，给出带出处的结论。结论对不对，以源码为准。 - **并发：一半路由，一半判定。** `model_interleaving_scan` 挖出声明并按 family 路由（线程→TSan/Helgrind/CBMC/TLA+，中断→RTOS 感知分析，异步→TLA+/UPPAAL 加运行时检查）。**但共享位置不再只是路由**：把 `shared` 与 `accesses` 交给 `model_compose_verify`，它会判定无序写（C4）与非原子更新/丢更新（C5）——那是一个能在模型上给出最短路见证的决定，不是某个检查的名字。源码级竞争、阻塞调用、漏 `await` 与锁是否跨整个操作持有，仍在路由的另一半。 - **图的审查不等于代码审查。** 图与它声称的模型一致，只说明图画对了。代码是不是这样，还得对着源码核验。 ## 环境要求 - 逐版本的安装 / 挂载 / 启动 / 卸载证据在 [DSH-COMPATIBILITY.md](DSH-COMPATIBILITY.md)。 - DeepSeek Harness：准入看 `package.json` 的 `peerDependencies`——插件管理器按它决定装不装得下，`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` 只是记录实测结论。逐版本兼容性是**实测项**，没实测过的版本一律标 `unknown`。 - Node.js：`>=20`。 - 无 Python 依赖，无网络调用。 ## 权限与数据 - 运行时只读包内的 `skills/` 目录（用于注册技能），不读凭据，也不联网。 - 工具只处理你传进来的模型、图与文件路径。报告里只有它算出的结论与哈希。 - 导出到外部检查器（UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN）时只写你指定的文件。 ## 故障排查 - **技能不可见**：确认 DSH 版本支持 `ctx.skills` 与 Agent Skills 发现，并在安装后重启 profile。 - **工具不在**：先查 `enabled`（可能是 `false`），再看插件管理器是否真的装上了（`--dump-config` 里有没有本插件的行）。 - **插件管理器拒绝安装**：确认 `@deepseek-ai/*` 在 `peerDependencies` 里，而不是 `dependencies`。 - **某个图族被拒绝**：这是设计行为。UML 2.5 的十四个图族在本构建里都有实现，所以拒绝永远是关于记号的：记号画不出这个视图，或画得出但读不回来。它按名拒绝并说明理由，不会交出错的模型。 ## 开发 ```bash npm install npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm run build # tsc → lib/（lib/ 必须与 src/ 同步提交） npm run test:engine # 全部回归套件，含记忆门禁 npm run test:full # 端到端合并套件 npm run lint:md # markdownlint，与 CI 同一个版本 npm run bump -- # 同步声明版本 npm run bump -- --check # 版本一致性 npm run bump -- --audit # 版本引用审计 ``` 外部检查器往返（`tests/external/run.mjs`）会调用真实的 `spin` 与 `gcc` 跑一遍导出结果。工具不在 PATH 上时整组自动跳过——跳过不算通过。要指向别处的可执行文件，用两个环境变量： ```bash MODEL_EVERYTHING_SPIN=/path/to/spin MODEL_EVERYTHING_GCC=/path/to/gcc npm run test:engine ``` 插件自己不调用 `spin`、`gcc`、UPPAAL、TLA+ 或 PRISM：`model_export` 只写出它们能读的输入。 约定、目录地图与硬约束见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)。项目记忆（调研结论、架构决定、交接）的入口在 [.github/memory/MEMORY.md](.github/memory/MEMORY.md)。 想参与：两种来件的结构不同——**有出处的改进**（要引用方法、点名改哪个码、说明是改判定还是加信号，并附最邻近反例与一条能红的变异）与**运行中遇到的问题**（要原样引用报告、给最小复现），分别见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) 与 [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/)。 ## 参考文献 各条检查背后的已发表工作——以及哪些检查**没有**已发表来源——收在 [docs/references.md](docs/references.md)。每一条都从仓库里 `Provenance` 表**逐字提取**（生成器 `docs/references/generate.mjs`），并标注它在哪个文件里被引用。这份清单存在的意义是把「已发表方法」与「本仓库自己的约定」分开：多数检查是后者，而把约定当成引用写出来，比说明它是约定更糟。 ## 许可证与安全 MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。安全策略见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。 ## 赞助 本插件以 MIT 许可证开源。如果它节省了你的时间，可以在[爱发电](https://afdian.com/a/amethystluna)赞助开发。 赞助完全自愿，不影响许可证，也不改变任何功能。
